summary: Audit logs SIEM export intermittently failing for S3 sink (exporter retries/backpressure)
description:
Customer reports intermittent failures exporting Audit Logs to their S3 bucket (SIEM ingest path). Export appears to work for a period, then fails for ~10–30 minutes, then resumes. Customer sees gaps and repeated delivery attempts.

Issue summary:
- S3 sink export intermittently fails with transient AWS errors; exporter does not sufficiently back off and can thrash, resulting in dropped/expired batches and delayed delivery.

Impact:
- Audit log export gaps / delays in customer S3 bucket.
- Customer has procurement/security review in progress; needs reliability story + fix ETA.

Customer context:
- Export destination: Customer-managed S3 bucket (cross-account role assumption).
- Format: JSONL
- Delivery: near-real-time (minutes)

Environment:
- Redwood Hosted: prod us-east
- Exporter: audit-log-exporter (multi-tenant), S3 sink enabled for customer org

Customer-provided examples:
- They observe missing objects for prefixes like: s3://<bucket>/redwood-audit/org_<org_id>/dt=2025-06-23/hr=14/
- Gaps correlate with exporter errors.

Redwood logs (support excerpt):
- 2025-06-23T14:22:11.391Z level=error component=audit-log-exporter sink=s3 org_id=org_2f3a*** request_id=alexp_01J1B*** msg="s3 put_object failed" error="RequestTimeout: Your socket connection to the server was not read from or written to within the timeout period. idle timeout"
- 2025-06-23T14:22:11.392Z level=warn  component=audit-log-exporter sink=s3 org_id=org_2f3a*** msg="retrying export" attempt=1 backoff_ms=250
- 2025-06-23T14:22:11.701Z level=warn  component=audit-log-exporter sink=s3 org_id=org_2f3a*** msg="retrying export" attempt=2 backoff_ms=250
- 2025-06-23T14:22:11.982Z level=error component=audit-log-exporter sink=s3 org_id=org_2f3a*** msg="export failed after retries" attempts=3 error="RequestTimeout"
- 2025-06-23T14:22:12.010Z level=warn  component=audit-log-exporter msg="batch expired before export; dropping" batch_id=bat_7b0*** age_ms=612345

Notes:
- Backoff appears too aggressive/flat; retries occur without exponential backoff/jitter.
- When S3 has transient slowdown/throttling, exporter churn increases queue lag and may drop expired batches.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Enable S3 sink for an org with moderate audit event throughput.
2) Introduce transient S3 failures (simulate via network fault injection or reduce timeouts) / or reproduce during AWS RequestTimeout windows.
3) Observe exporter retry loop and batch expirations; verify gaps in exported objects.

Requested by customer:
- Confirmation this is known + ETA.
- Assurance on retry/DLQ behavior and whether gaps can be re-driven.
- Guidance on recommended S3 bucket/IAM configuration and any AWS limits.

Attachments:
- None (customer pasted snippets into email; summarized above).
comments: 2025-06-24 09:18 (Rachel Kim, Support) — Opened ticket from customer email: S3 export intermittently failing; customer seeing missing audit logs in bucket. Marking P1 due to enterprise blocker and potential compliance impact. Looping in SIEM/export owner (Svetlana) and SRE (Rafael) for investigation. Slack ref: #support thread "Hightower S3 audit export gaps".

2025-06-24 10:02 (Svetlana Petrenko, Assignee) — Acknowledged. Pulling exporter logs for org_2f3a*** and checking per-sink metrics. Initial hypothesis: transient S3 RequestTimeout/SlowDown + exporter retry policy too tight (no exp backoff/jitter), causing burst retries and eventual batch expiry/drops. Will confirm whether we have DLQ/rehydration for S3 sink in current build.

2025-06-24 11:10 (Rafael Mendes, SRE) — Checked Grafana (audit-log-exporter) in us-east: spikes in s3_export_errors_total and elevated export_lag_seconds p95 aligning with customer’s reported windows. Not seeing full pipeline ingest issues; failure isolated to S3 sink worker. Suggest we treat "export failed" as retryable longer and add dead-letter queue for durable re-drive rather than dropping expired batches.

2025-06-24 12:35 (Svetlana Petrenko) — Confirmed current behavior: exporter retries 3x with fixed 250ms backoff; after that we mark batch failed and (depending on age) it can hit "expired" and be dropped. For S3 transient errors, this is too harsh. Drafting fix: exponential backoff + jitter, classify AWS errors (RequestTimeout, SlowDown, 5xx) as retryable, add DLQ for failed batches with periodic re-drive. Will implement in audit-log-exporter repo; targeting PR by EOD tomorrow.

2025-06-24 13:05 (Rachel Kim, Support) — Customer update sent: We reproduced/confirmed exporter-side retry behavior; working on reliability patch (backoff + DLQ) and will provide ETA within 24h. Asked customer for: bucket region, any S3 access logs during failure windows, and whether they require exactly-once vs at-least-once semantics (we are at-least-once).

2025-06-25 16:22 (Svetlana Petrenko) — PR opened: sources/github/audit-log-exporter/pr_232.json. Changes include: exponential backoff with jitter (up to 2 minutes), circuit-breaker style backpressure per sink, DLQ for batches that exceed max retry window, and structured error reporting (error_class=retryable/non_retryable). Also added per-sink metrics: s3_retry_attempts, s3_dlq_enqueued_total, s3_dlq_redrive_total.

2025-06-26 09:40 (Aisha Bello, SRE/Observability) — Added/updated dashboards and alerts for exporter lag + drop rate, including per-sink panels (S3/Webhook) and a DLQ backlog panel. PR reference: sources/github/observability-pack/pr_418.json.

2025-06-26 11:15 (Rafael Mendes, SRE) — Staging validation: simulated S3 RequestTimeout; exporter backs off correctly now, no batch expirations observed, and DLQ captures prolonged failures. Lag increases but recovers; no drops in exported_count. Recommend rollout canary in us-east prod for affected orgs first.

2025-06-27 14:05 (Svetlana Petrenko) — PR merged and released as audit-log-exporter v1.9.2. Rolled out to prod us-east with canary (10% workers) starting 13:40, expanded to 100% at 14:00 after stable metrics. Watching s3_export_errors_total and export_lag_seconds; both trending down; DLQ remains near-zero. No new drop logs.

2025-06-28 09:30 (Rachel Kim, Support) — Customer confirms new objects arriving continuously; they still see a gap from 2025-06-23 14:22–14:41. Asked Engineering if we can re-drive missing window; awaiting answer. Also provided customer guidance: ensure bucket is in same region as exporter (us-east-1), allow PutObject/ListBucket with correct prefix, and avoid overly restrictive lifecycle rules that expire objects quickly.

2025-07-01 10:12 (Svetlana Petrenko) — We cannot retroactively reconstruct already-dropped batches from 6/23 window (pre-fix) unless events still exist in primary audit store beyond retention and we run a manual backfill job. For this customer, events are retained in primary store; we can run a targeted backfill for the missing time range into their S3 prefix (will produce at-least-once duplicates outside the gap if overlap). I can run a one-time re-export via internal tool; needs approval from Security/Compliance for customer export action log + change record.

2025-07-01 11:00 (Marcus Lin, Security Eng) — Approved one-time customer backfill export for the requested window provided: (1) action is recorded as an internal admin audit event, (2) scoped to org_id and time window only, (3) ticket includes customer confirmation of target bucket/prefix. Rachel, please get explicit written confirmation from customer on window + destination.

2025-07-02 09:05 (Rachel Kim, Support) — Customer confirmed (email) destination bucket/prefix and window. Svetlana executed one-time backfill export for 2025-06-23 14:15–14:50 UTC. Customer confirms gap filled and SIEM ingest is green. Proceeding to resolve ticket.
resolution: Fixed in audit-log-exporter v1.9.2 via improved retry/backoff and durability: exponential backoff with jitter, per-sink backpressure, and DLQ support to prevent batch drops during transient S3 failures. Rolled out to prod us-east on 2025-06-27. Performed one-time scoped backfill export for the customer’s missing window on 2025-07-02 after approval. Customer confirmed export reliability and gap remediation.
customer_facing_next_steps: Monitor S3 export for 7 days; customer to confirm no further gaps. Redwood to provide updated reliability note for security review: at-least-once delivery semantics, retry/DLQ behavior, and recommended S3 configuration. If AWS SlowDown/RequestTimeout rates increase, customer can expect increased delivery lag but not drops under normal conditions.
internal_follow_ups: Document DLQ and re-drive procedure in runbook (audit-log-delivery-lag-runbook) with approval steps for one-time backfills.
Add automated chaos test for S3 sink transient failures in exporter CI.
Review batch expiration policy across all sinks to ensure retry windows are compatible with enterprise SLOs.
